junction.name: Bruckner Boulevard & Hunts Point Avenue, New York City

claims.text: Bruckner Boulevard & Hunts Point Avenue had 75 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 17 pedestrians injured, 1 cyclist injured and 0 people killed.
These counts are Bruckner Boulevard & Hunts Point Avenue's own: the city's record places 79 of the 310 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $5.1 million a year.
30% of crashes here involved a truck or bus, against 16% at the city's priority junctions.
Held up on later years: a truck or bus was involved in 31% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 16% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search).
Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading south in 31% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 17% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).
Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 2.3 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $770,000 a year.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 1.2 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $401,000 a year; check on site: the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 is responsible for Bruckner Expressway (I 278), Arthur V. Sheridan Boulevard (NY 895) (owner recorded in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory).
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Bruckner Boulevard, Hunts Point Avenue (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 17, New York City Council; Bronx Community Board 2.
A request letter to the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 and the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11; the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 17, New York City Council; Bronx Community Board 2
Subject: Request for safety review at Bruckner Boulevard & Hunts Point Avenue

Dear colleagues at NYSDOT Region 11 and NYC DOT,

I am writing to ask each agency to carry out a safety study at the junction of Bruckner Boulevard and Hunts Point Avenue, and to consider fixes on the roads it owns.

The official record for the 5 years from 31 October 2021 shows 199 crashes, including 75 injury crashes. 17 pedestrians and 1 cyclist were injured, and 0 people were killed in the modes recorded as cyclist, motorist, and pedestrian. This is a city priority location. Using the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the harm is valued at $5.1 million per year. In that period there is no recorded safety treatment; the latest recorded project was Bruckner Blvd at Hunts Pt Ave (INT) in 2015.

Please consider these low-cost fixes on the roads you are responsible for:

• Reflective backplates on the traffic signals (FHWA-cited). Expected to prevent about 2.3 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $770,000 in harm per year, paying for itself if it costs under $5.4 million.

• Longer yellow signal times, if on-site check shows the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice (evidence needs a site check). Expected to prevent about 1.2 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $401,000 in harm per year, paying for itself if it costs under $2.8 million.

Where the city installed a leading pedestrian interval (a walk signal a few seconds before the green) at 1,651 intersections, pedestrian injury crashes fell 17% (95% interval 11% to 22%) compared with intersections that got it later; a stricter check against fake programs is less certain. Please check on site whether a turning movement is present before considering this.

Thank you for considering this request.

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
